school_name: Columbia University in the City of New York
title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
description: Explore Columbia's campus and the surrounding Morningside Heights neighborhood with these social activities and spaces that require no admission or purchase.

cards.title: Lounge on the Low Steps
cards.subtitle: Morningside Campus Centerpiece
cards.notes: Gather on the granite steps for people-watching and sunbathing. This iconic social hub is the primary meeting spot for students between classes.
cards.short_summary: The university's central outdoor social gathering spot.
cards.evidence_claim: The Low Library steps are a natural gathering place for students and a social agora in good weather.
cards.access_notes: Open 24/7 to CUID holders; public access currently requires guest registration or neighbor QR code.

cards.title: Visit the Wallach Art Gallery
cards.subtitle: Lenfest Center for the Arts
cards.notes: Explore contemporary art exhibitions and MFA thesis shows in this sleek Manhattanville space. It is the university's premier public visual arts venue.
cards.short_summary: A free public art gallery showcasing contemporary works.
cards.evidence_claim: The Wallach Art Gallery is free and open to the public Wednesday through Sunday from 12 to 6 PM.
cards.source_title: PLAN YOUR VISIT - Wallach Art Gallery
cards.access_notes: Open Wednesday-Sunday, 12:00 PM - 6:00 PM. No CUID required for entry.

cards.title: Attend a Sacred Music Concert
cards.subtitle: Historic Campus Chapel
cards.notes: Listen to world-class organists and chamber ensembles in a landmark setting. Concerts are held regularly throughout the academic year.
cards.short_summary: Free professional music performances in a historic landmark.
cards.evidence_claim: Sacred Music presents free concerts at St. Paul's Chapel that are open to the public with advance registration.
cards.access_notes: Concerts typically start at 6:00 PM. Non-affiliates must register by 11:00 AM the day prior.

cards.title: Study in the Butler Stacks
cards.subtitle: Main Humanities Library
cards.notes: Find a quiet carrel or a grand reading room in Columbia's largest library. It is a quintessential campus experience for late-night academic sessions.
cards.short_summary: The primary campus library offering vast study spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: Butler Library houses collections in humanities and history and provides numerous service points and study spaces.
cards.access_notes: Open late; CUID required for entry. Visitors require an appointment or temporary pass.

cards.title: Watch the Sunset at Riverside
cards.subtitle: Hudson River Waterfront
cards.notes: Walk two blocks west of campus to enjoy river views and green lawns. The park hosts free yoga and movie screenings during the summer months.
cards.short_summary: A scenic waterfront park perfect for outdoor recreation.
cards.evidence_claim: Summer on the Hudson offers over 400 free events including movies and yoga in Riverside Park.
cards.source_title: Summer on the Hudson - Riverside Park Conservancy
cards.access_notes: Public park open daily from 6:00 AM to 1:00 AM.

cards.title: Relax by the Waterfall
cards.subtitle: 113th Street and Morningside Ave
cards.notes: Visit the pond and waterfall at the base of the cliffs. This peaceful spot is ideal for a nature break just steps from the eastern campus gates.
cards.short_summary: A scenic natural feature in the adjacent community park.
cards.evidence_claim: Morningside Park features a waterfall and pond that host community festivals and jazz concerts.
cards.access_notes: Public park open daily from 6:00 AM to 1:00 AM.

cards.title: Find Peace in Earl Hall
cards.subtitle: Center for Religious Life
cards.notes: Use the quiet rooms for meditation or prayer. This historic building serves as a sanctuary for students of all faith traditions on campus.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated space for spiritual life and quiet reflection.
cards.evidence_claim: Earl Hall provides prayer and meditation spaces and is the home of the University Chaplain.
cards.access_notes: CUID required for campus entry; building accessible via south entrance facing Lewisohn Hall.

cards.title: Explore NYC Museums for Free
cards.subtitle: Student Arts Initiative
cards.notes: Use your CUID to get free admission to over 30 museums, including MoMA and the Met. It is one of the most valuable perks of being a Columbia student.
cards.short_summary: Free access to major NYC cultural institutions for students.
cards.evidence_claim: The Passport to Museums program provides current Columbia students free admission to over 30 NYC museums with a valid CUID.
cards.source_title: Museums - Arts Initiative at Columbia University
cards.access_notes: Requires a valid CUID with a current semester validation sticker.

cards.title: Hang Out at The Forum
cards.subtitle: Manhattanville Campus Hub
cards.notes: Enjoy the open, modern ground floor with plenty of seating and free Wi-Fi. This glass-walled space is designed to bridge the university and the community.
cards.short_summary: A modern, transparent community and university gathering space.
cards.evidence_claim: The Forum is an open space with glass walls and a clean, modern look available for study and gathering.
cards.source_title: Where to Study at Columbia University - University Life
cards.access_notes: Ground floor is generally open to the public during regular building hours.

cards.title: Stroll Along College Walk
cards.subtitle: 116th Street Pedestrian Path
cards.notes: Walk the brick-paved path between Broadway and Amsterdam. In winter, the trees are famously lit with white lights, creating a festive atmosphere.
cards.short_summary: The central pedestrian thoroughfare of the Morningside campus.
cards.evidence_claim: College Walk connects Broadway and Amsterdam and is the heart of the Morningside campus.
cards.access_notes: CUID required for entry; local neighbors can request access via a specific QR code program.
